subject: neutrophils
correct: Suspected neutropenic sepsis (unwell or febrile during/after systemic anticancer treatment) = IMMEDIATE referral/emergency assessment via the 24-hour acute oncology hotline or 999/A&E; antibiotics within 1 hour in hospital; do not wait for FBC (NICE CG151 1.2.1; NG253; UKONS triage uses ≥37.5°C)

fixes.old: Chemotherapy within 6 weeks with fever → Same-day neutropenic sepsis pathway.
fixes.new: Recent chemotherapy (within 6 weeks) with fever or feeling unwell → Immediate neutropenic sepsis pathway (acute oncology hotline / 999; do not wait for FBC).

fixes.old: • Neutropenic risk (chemotherapy within 6 weeks + fever) → Same-day
fixes.new: • Neutropenic risk (chemotherapy within 6 weeks + fever or unwell) → Immediate acute oncology hotline / 999

fixes.old: or on neutropenia-causing drugs → Same-day acute oncology; do not wait for FBC.
fixes.new: or on neutropenia-causing drugs → Immediate acute oncology hotline / 999; do not wait for FBC.

fixes.old: FEBRILE NEUTROPENIA: temperature ≥38°C or feeling unwell during chemotherapy = SAME-DAY oncology/haematology assessment (A&E if out of hours).
fixes.new: FEBRILE NEUTROPENIA: temperature ≥37.5°C or feeling unwell during chemotherapy = IMMEDIATE assessment via the 24-hour acute oncology/chemotherapy hotline (999/A&E if very unwell or the hotline cannot be reached).

note: CG151 says refer suspected neutropenic sepsis immediately; 'same-day' understates a 1-hour-to-antibiotics emergency and conflicts with the site's own neutropenic-sepsis, leucopenia, pancytopenia and summaries/breast-cancer pages ('Immediately', 999/hotline, ≥37.5°C). The 6-week window is wider than NG253's 30 days, so it is safe and is kept. Search index JSON (assets/search/idx-pathway.json) may carry the old snippet; regenerate it rather than hand-editing.

subject: neutrophils
correct: NICE CG151: piperacillin with tazobactam monotherapy as initial empirical therapy; the BNF/SPC dose in neutropenic patients is 4.5 g IV every 6 hours (adjust for renal function); local protocol applies. UKONS's triage tool does not specify an antibiotic.

fixes.old: The UK Oncology Nursing Society (UKONS) neutropenic sepsis pathway specifies piperacillin-tazobactam (Tazocin) 4.5 g IV every 8 hours as first-line in most centres.
fixes.new: NICE CG151 recommends piperacillin-tazobactam (Tazocin) monotherapy as initial empirical treatment, given in hospital within 1 hour; the dose follows the hospital protocol and BNF (commonly 4.5 g IV every 6 hours in neutropenic patients, adjusted for renal function).

note: Wrong frequency (every 8 h is the general-infection dose; the neutropenic dose is every 6 h) and wrong attribution (UKONS triage tool gives no antibiotic regimen; CG151 sets the drug choice). Hospital-only fact, but it is a dose statement.

subject: prednisolone
group: exogenous steroid sick-day rules | no-extra-dose threshold
correct: NICE NG243 (2024): during intercurrent illness give at least 10 mg prednisolone a day (in 1–2 doses), so a patient already on ≥10 mg needs no increase (the site's sick-day-rules page, its print twin and NHS Scotland use this). The Society for Endocrinology leaflet 'Oral steroids for lung disease' uses ≥15 mg (and steps doses >5 to <15 mg up to 15 mg).
note: OWNER: cases/addisons-disease.html (line ~557 table row 'already on prednisolone ≥15 mg/day', and line ~625 'if already on ≥15 mg/day, no extra steroid is needed') uses 15 mg, while tools/management/sick-day-rules.html, sick-day-rules-print.html and summaries/sick-day-rules.html use 10 mg (NG243). Both have a UK source. Suggest aligning the Addison's case to NG243 (≥10 mg: no extra, split into 2 doses), with a note that some SfE patient materials use 15 mg. The two thresholds differ only for patients on 10–14 mg/day.
